features.method: Derived: a 7 m diameter circle (32-gon, radius 3.5 m) centred on the centroid (45.206099 N, 5.692848 E) of the near-circular OSM outline of the reactor building (way 191447189; vertex radii 29.76-29.96 m about that centroid). The ILL engineering paper states that the foundation raft of the cylindrical reactor building 'supports a concrete cylinder 7 m in diameter ... This cylinder is the core of the reactor' at 'the centre of the raft'; the raft is circular and carries the cylindrical building, so the building centre is taken as the raft centre. A circle is drawn here only because the source gives the cylinder's diameter and the centre follows from a sourced circular building.
features.name: ILL reactor core cylinder (7 m diameter) at the centre of the reactor building

provenance.locator: ILL engineering paper (IGORR 10, 2005), section 2; centre = centroid of OSM way 191447189
provenance.note: The circle is the footprint of the cylinder that houses the core, not of the fuel element (which is smaller). Position rests on the reactor building being concentric with its foundation raft.
provenance.quote: The centre of the raft supports a concrete cylinder 7 m in diameter, 2 m thick and 15 m in height. This cylinder is the core of the reactor

map.name: Institut Laue-Langevin — reactor building and guide halls on the EPN campus

summary.plain: The Institut Laue-Langevin in Grenoble, drawn to scale: the 60-metre domed reactor building with its core cylinder, the two neutron-guide halls beside it, and the shared EPN campus boundary. The Ricochet detector is known only as 8.8 metres from the core, so it is not drawn.

unlocated.backlog: Find a Ricochet installation drawing or paper that gives the CryoCube room position or its bearing from the core (the Ricochet commissioning paper or an ILL experimental-area plan), then place it on the circle of radius 8.8 m about the core cylinder drawn here.
unlocated.reason: Ricochet CryoCube: sourced only as 8.8 m from the reactor core ('8.8 meters away from the 58 MW research nuclear reactor core'). That fixes a distance, not a position: no fetched source gives the bearing or room, so the detector can lie anywhere on a 8.8 m circle about the core and is not drawn. Its site, the reactor building, is drawn.
